The C callback has no Swift captures. Its TimeInterval context lives within synchronous withUnsafeMutablePointer scope. Scope defer replaces the handler with sqlite3_busy_timeout(3000) before the stack pointer becomes invalid, for success and thrown errors.
The callback only reads its deadline/monotonic time and sleeps at most the remaining allowance. It checks the deadline both before and after sleep and never reenters or closes SQLite.

Both prepare and all step callbacks share one deadline. Immediate-BUSY outer retries also check the same deadline after their sleep. Only WAL initialization and SQLITE_BUSY are retried; each attempt finalizes its statement.

realRisksAndLimits: The fix prohibits new contention waits/retries after the deadline when execution resumes; it cannot force execution while a process is stopped or guarantee an absolute whole-process three-second return during OS suspension, scheduling stalls, filesystem work or successful I/O.

The unchanged <4s assertion remains a useful guard under normal runner scheduling. It is not proof that arbitrary OS stalls are bounded. A later failure must be investigated using its actual evidence, not hidden by threshold expansion.
